analysis.title: GS Basics: Pivotal. Rates Resilient. Heavy Tech Selling. (19 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Futures are sharply higher, led by the NDX. Asia is weak: a TSMC-exposed basket is down 8% and Asian data center names are under pressure.

New BIS rules tighten advanced AI chip licensing across parts of Asia and Brazil and restrict offshore compute access for Chinese customers. The note says the effect on delayed projects, displaced demand and excess infrastructure capacity is hard to quantify and was not fully priced in Asia.

Positioning is the offset. Two months of aggressive selling have left valuations depressed across global semis, so it does not take much good news to squeeze. If the BIS implications can be compartmentalized, that is encouraging.
Bonds rallied despite a hawkish Waller, the Fed minutes and ECB regulatory noise. The back end was well bid, the curve bull flattened and the front end was broadly unchanged.
Australia is singled out: a big jobs miss, the 2yr rallying hard and cuts starting to price. This is now potentially signaling the end of the hiking cycle.

The market is increasingly pricing weaker growth as capex expectations fall, commodities roll over and inflationary pressure fades. The note compares this to the end of 2018: the same late-cycle slowdown but very different policy implications.
The rates price action was encouraging and suggests a lot of policy is already in the price. Equity internals are very defensive and commodities now point the same way.

A strong dollar, elevated real rates and attractive all-in credit yields compete with gold and precious metals. The note calls it a spending glut, not a savings glut, which is a less supportive backdrop for precious metals and multiples with the Fed tightening.
China adds a headwind: weak growth, Shanghai equities near their lows and little sign of recovery. Potential restrictions on AI and data center investment compound it.

Copper has become a proxy for the AI infrastructure theme, so its resilience is hard to reconcile with collapsing AI infrastructure equities. Precious and industrial metals, grains, gasoline and diesel are all under pressure, a broad disinflationary impulse that could change the rates narrative.
SPX is precariously holding its 200-day moving average. Street gamma positioning is meant to be very short, but vol was soggy yesterday for the first time in a while, particularly after VIX expiry.

With VIX in the mid 20s and Thanksgiving next week, there is a meaningful potential tailwind if the market stabilizes. If rates cooperate, there is a legitimate bull case for equities because a lot of the AI issues are already in price.
Today's calendar: Walmart earnings, jobless claims, the Philly Fed and the 10yr TIPS auction at 18:00. Watch JPY approaching 160 and tech broadly.
earnings_insights: Walmart reports earnings on 19 Nov 2026. The note gives no estimate or result figures.
